description: Defects planted into a staged copy of the fixture, each an exact-string edit. Every one is a place where the correct behaviour is defined by the Skerry protocol's own rules rather than by anything a reader can derive from the surrounding code, so only a tester who knows those rules knows what to pin. The suite the repository ships catches none of them.

defects.title: A computed checksum of zero is sent as zero
defects.rationale: Only a payload whose weighted sum lands on one residue reaches the branch, so a suite that round-trips ordinary payloads never sees it.

defects.title: An odd-length payload is padded with zero instead of the protocol's pad byte
defects.rationale: The frame still round-trips, because the length field excludes the pad. Only a test that pins the encoded bytes of an odd-length frame notices.

defects.title: The broadcast node id is accepted as a frame source
defects.rationale: A frame claiming to come from the broadcast address decodes cleanly. Needs a hand-built frame with that node, which no encode call can produce.

defects.title: The sentinel raw value is reported as a real depth
defects.rationale: The most negative 12-bit value means no reading was taken. Without the check it becomes a depth of about minus 292 metres.

defects.title: Sequence order is a plain comparison, so the wrap past 4095 is rejected
defects.rationale: Every ordinary run of increasing sequence numbers behaves identically. The defect shows only when the counter wraps from near 4095 to near 0.

defects.title: A RESET does not forget the last sequence number
defects.rationale: After a reset the stream restarts from a low number and must be accepted. Needs a sequence of frames, a reset, then a lower sequence number.
